messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: GW-502-Spike (ID gw-2026-03-15-01) — api-gateway error rate (502/504) > 15% across edge proxies in the last 5m. Pager sent to on-call.
Alex Chen: I'm on it, waking up stack now. which regions?
Maria Gomez: seeing it in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, small blip in ap-southeast-1. traffic surge started ~10:11 UTC.
Samir Patel: Confirmed. Grafana shows latency spike followed by 502s coming from origin pool B (ingress-backend-b).
Katie Li: Support reporting initial customer complaints — a handful of API failures for high-throughput customers. Not yet widespread.
Jit Rao: Logs show upstream 504 timeouts when proxy tried to reach origin. sample from edge: \"upstream_response_time\": \"10.2\", \"status\": 504
Alex Chen: Can someone run a quick curl through edge to reproduce? I want minimal repro.
observability-bot: Synthetic check failing for /v1/generate on edge-proxy-us-east-1 (502) — started 10:12:34 UTC.
Samir Patel: repro from my laptop: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` -> 502. attaching headers.
Maria Gomez: Rolling back last gateway rollout candidate? We had a canary push ~09:50.
Alex Chen: I rolled back the gateway config canary at 10:18 but error rate didn't drop immediately. Might be sticky connections or upstream backlog.
Jit Rao: Suggest routing traffic away from origin pool B -> A for now. Can we flip routing on LB?
Samir Patel: Starting a temporary route diversion. patching traffic-steering to prefer origin-A for 50% now.
Alex Chen: Add circuit-breaker on origin-B to fail fast (shorten connect timeout) so proxy returns 503 quickly instead of waiting and causing queues.
Katie Li: Coordinating with Support: collecting affected customer IDs and time windows. I'll post update to CS pager after we have metrics.
observability-bot: Error rate dropped from 18% -> 7% after partial diversion (10:25 UTC). latency still elevated.
Maria Gomez: Looks like backlog draining. origin-B pods show OOM-kill events around 10:09-10:15 in k8s logs.
Samir Patel: Scaling origin-B by +3 replicas and restarting crashed pods. k8s commands: ```kubectl scale deploy origin-b --replicas=7 -n inbound && kubectl rollout restart deploy/origin-b -n inbound```
Alex Chen: Good. Keep diversion until health checks stable for 10m. Also enable prefix KV cache at edge for hot routes to reduce origin load.
Jit Rao: Enabled cache for /v1/generate prefix with 30s TTL on edge-proxy us-east-1.
Katie Li: Support update: initial PSAT customers impacted: 4 customers with retries surfaced, one raised severity 2. I'm drafting message for affected accounts.
Alex Chen: Next steps: 1) Monitor error rate for 15m, 2) keep diversion and circuit-breaker, 3) watch memory churn on origin-B, 4) post incident timeline for CS.
Maria Gomez: I'm going to dig into why origin-B pods OOMed — maybe new model char limit or memory leak from recent lib update.
Samir Patel: logs: `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError` inside tokenization worker on some pods. pointing to tokenizer v2.3. We should consider pinning tokenizer to v2.2 for origin-B if needed.
observability-bot: 15m rolling check: error rate 2.1% (10:45 UTC), latency trending down.
Alex Chen: OK, leaving this thread open until 11:00 UTC for confirmation. If numbers stay good we'll close. Katie, please escalate any customer facing issues to SEs.
Katie Li: Will do. posting to support with ETA and mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
Support: Customer-facing note ready to send once we confirm stable. will coordinate postmortem template.
Maria Gomez: capturing action items: rollback tokenizer v2.3 on origin-B if reoccurs, add memory alerts, investigate root cause.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Good mitigation flow — saved us from a wider outage. :tada:
incidents-bot: Incident gw-2026-03-15-01 transitioned to \"monitoring\" (no active mitigation) at 10:47 UTC.
observability-bot: Final snapshot: error rate settled <1% at 10:56 UTC.
Alex Chen: closing thread in 10m if all quiet. Thanks all. :wave:
